name: Data Table (Sortable, Paginated, Filterable)
description: A data table for browsing records: a real table with a caption and row headers, sortable headers with buttons and aria-sort on the sorted column only, a filter field, pages whose Previous and Next keep focus, and a selection kept across pages, with a header checkbox for the page.

tokens.note: Suggested defaults. The project's design tokens and existing components win.

layout.layering: A sticky header row is a sticky bar of the project's layering scale; the table needs no other layer.

aiAgentInstructions.summary: Build or extend a data table for browsing records: a real table with a caption and row headers, sortable headers with a button inside each and aria-sort on the sorted column only, a filter field, pages, and a selection kept across pages and the filter, with a header checkbox for the page. Use the parts the task needs. Build on the project's table component, or the table library it already uses, when it has a suitable one. Implement only what the task needs, keep existing APIs, and match the project's styling and tokens. The project's conventions win for styling and visual defaults; if one conflicts with an accessibility or correctness requirement in this guide, ask the user instead of choosing silently. Target WCAG 2.2 AA.
keyFeatures: A <table> with a <caption>, column headers, and a row header for the cell that names each row; a plain table, not a grid
A button inside each sortable <th>, aria-sort on the sorted column only, and comparisons by type, with Intl.Collator for text
A labelled filter field: back to page 1, only the latest answer, and the number of matches said once typing pauses
Pages whose Previous and Next use aria-disabled at the ends, with aria-current="page" on the current one
A checkbox per row, named after it, and a header checkbox for the page; the selection kept across pages and the filter
Loading, empty, and error states in text; a wide table scrolling in a named region
implementationSteps: 1. Detect the framework and its version, the styling system, the tokens, and the existing components, including a table library (projectDetection). If the project already has a data table, configure or extend it to meet this guide instead of building another one, and keep its API.
2. Choose what the task needs: sorting, filtering, pages, selection, cards on phones. Leave out the rest.
3. Build the table (componentSpec.anatomy) and its sortable headers (frameworkPatterns.sortableHeaders).
4. Add the filter field and pages (implementationDetails.filtering, implementationDetails.pages).
5. Add selection and the toolbar (frameworkPatterns.pageSelection, implementationDetails.selection).
6. Add the loading, empty, and error states, and phones (implementationDetails.states, implementationDetails.phones).
7. Check the result against testingChecklist with a keyboard, a screen reader, a phone, and 200% zoom, and run the project's existing tests and checks.

componentSpec.goal: Let people find, order, and act on records quickly, with a keyboard or a screen reader as well as a pointer, without acting on rows they didn't mean to.

anatomy.hierarchy: status region | filter bar | selection toolbar (space reserved) | scroll region (named by the caption) → table → caption | thead: header checkbox, column headers with sort buttons | tbody: rows with a checkbox, a row header, and cells | pagination

slotNotes.table: It's a real <table>. A <caption> names it, or aria-labelledby points to its heading. Column headers are <th scope="col">, and the cell that identifies a row, such as a name, is a <th scope="row">, so screen readers say whose row a cell is in.
slotNotes.plainTable: It's a plain table, not a grid: Tab moves between its controls (sort buttons, checkboxes, links), and rows and cells aren't focusable. Arrow-key navigation between cells belongs to the grid pattern (role="grid", one Tab stop, editing keys), which this guide doesn't cover.
slotNotes.scrollRegion: A table wider than its container scrolls inside a region with role="region", named by the caption, and tabindex="0", so keyboard users can scroll to columns that have nothing focusable.
slotNotes.sortButton: A sortable column has a <button> inside its <th>, named by the column's name; the header cell itself can't take focus. As in the APG sortable table example, the caption says that the column buttons sort.
slotNotes.ariaSort: aria-sort ("ascending" or "descending") is only on the sorted column's <th>. The other headers have none; ARIA allows one sorted header at a time.
slotNotes.rowCheckbox: Each row has a checkbox named after the row ("Select Émile Zola"), and the header has one for the page ("Select all customers on this page"). The checkbox is the one control: rows get neither tabindex nor aria-selected, which belong to the grid pattern.
slotNotes.headerCheckbox: The selection is kept by row id across pages and the filter. The header checkbox shows only this page: checked when every row on it is selected, and partly checked (indeterminate, read as "mixed") when some are.
slotNotes.status: One polite status region, in the page before it changes, for sorting, the number of matches, page changes, and loading.

sort.description: The sorted column and its direction ("ascending" or "descending"), or none; mirrored in aria-sort on that column only.

page.description: The current page, from 1. A new filter, sort, or page size goes back to 1.

pageSize.persistence: Optional: the app's preferences, under its own prefix

selected.description: The selected rows' ids, kept across pages and the filter.

dataState.description: Whether the rows are loading, loaded, empty, or failed.

interactions.accessibilityNotes: The sorted column reverses; another column sorts ascending. aria-sort stays on one header.
Only the latest answer fills the table; hidden rows stay selected.
Previous and Next at the ends are aria-disabled and ignore presses. If the view moves to the table, focus moves with it.
Only this page's rows; rows on other pages keep their state.
Asks first, naming the count, or offers undo.

responsiveBehavior.phones: Below 768 px, rows can become cards in a list (<ul>), each card's fields a description list (<dl>), with the row's name as the card's heading. The checkboxes stay, named after their rows; sorting moves to a "Sort by" select, and pagination to Previous and Next. When the columns need to be compared side by side, keep the table, scrolling in its region, instead.
responsiveBehavior.wideTables: A table wider than its container scrolls inside a region with role="region", named by the caption, and tabindex="0", so keyboard users can scroll to columns that have nothing focusable.

variants.filterable: One labelled filter field above the table ("Filter customers", an <input type="search">) narrows the rows by their text, in the browser or on the server.
variants.paginated: Below the table: Previous and Next, page numbers from 768 px, a "Rows per page" select (10, 25, 50, or 100), and a summary ("Showing 11–20 of 245").
variants.selectable: Row checkboxes, the header checkbox, and the selection toolbar.
variants.rowDetails: Row details: a disclosure button in the row ("Show details for Émile Zola") with aria-expanded, and the details in the next row, across all columns.

columns.shape: { id, header, type: "text" | "number" | "date", sortable?, rowHeader?, align?, hideBelowPx? }[]
columns.notes: One column is the row header, the one that names the row. type picks the comparison.

rows.notes: Stable ids, so the selection survives pages, sorting, and filtering.

animations.note: None needed. If rows animate when they reorder, they don't under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce.

requirements.1.3.1: A table with a caption, column headers, and row headers; the sorted column exposes aria-sort.
requirements.1.4.1: Selected rows and the sorted column are marked by more than color.
requirements.1.4.3: Cell text, headers, and muted text meet 4.5:1.
requirements.1.4.10: A wide table scrolls inside its region; the page doesn't scroll sideways.
requirements.1.4.11: Sort icons, checkbox edges, and focus indicators meet 3:1.
requirements.2.1.1: Sorting, filtering, pages, and selection all work from the keyboard.
requirements.2.4.3: Focus stays on Previous and Next at the ends, and moves to the table when the view does.
requirements.2.5.7: Anything done by dragging has a way without dragging.
requirements.4.1.2: Sort buttons, checkboxes, and the current page expose their names and states.
requirements.4.1.3: Sorting, matches, page changes, and loading are announced through one status region.

keyboardNavigation.tab: Moves through the filter, the toolbar, the scroll region, the sort buttons, the checkboxes and links in the rows, and the pagination.
keyboardNavigation.enterSpace: Sorts from a header button; checks a checkbox with Space.
keyboardNavigation.arrows: Left to the browser: they scroll the focused region; there is no cell navigation in a plain table.

sortedHeader.aria-sort: "ascending" or "descending", on the sorted column's th only

endButtons.aria-disabled: true on Previous on the first page and Next on the last

screenReader.cells: Moving along a row reads the column header and the row header with each cell.
screenReader.announcements: The status region says the sort, the number of matches, the page, and loading, once each.

focusManagement.pages: The status region says the new summary after a page change. If the page scrolls to the table's top, focus moves there too, to the caption or the table's heading (tabindex="-1"); otherwise the scroll position stays.
focusManagement.afterDelete: After rows are deleted, focus moves somewhere sensible nearby, such as the table's caption or the next row's checkbox, never the page's body.

implementationDetails.structure: It's a real <table>. A <caption> names it, or aria-labelledby points to its heading. Column headers are <th scope="col">, and the cell that identifies a row, such as a name, is a <th scope="row">, so screen readers say whose row a cell is in. It's a plain table, not a grid: Tab moves between its controls (sort buttons, checkboxes, links), and rows and cells aren't focusable. Arrow-key navigation between cells belongs to the grid pattern (role="grid", one Tab stop, editing keys), which this guide doesn't cover. Numbers are right-aligned, with tabular figures, and dates are <time datetime> elements. A table wider than its container scrolls inside a region with role="region", named by the caption, and tabindex="0", so keyboard users can scroll to columns that have nothing focusable. A cell that's cut short still gives a way to the whole value: let it wrap, or show it in the row's details.
implementationDetails.sorting: A sortable column has a <button> inside its <th>, named by the column's name; the header cell itself can't take focus. As in the APG sortable table example, the caption says that the column buttons sort. aria-sort ("ascending" or "descending") is only on the sorted column's <th>. The other headers have none; ARIA allows one sorted header at a time. A click on the sorted column reverses it, and a click on another column sorts it ascending. A third state that restores the original order is optional. Each column compares by its type: numbers as numbers, dates by their value, and text with Intl.Collator (numeric: true), so "Émile" sorts with E, and "Item 2" comes before "Item 10". The status region says how the table is sorted ("Sorted by Name, ascending"), and sorting goes back to page 1. With sorting on the server, send the column and the direction, set aria-sort when the answer arrives, and let only the latest answer fill the table.
implementationDetails.filtering: One labelled filter field above the table ("Filter customers", an <input type="search">) narrows the rows by their text, in the browser or on the server. Once typing pauses, the status region says how many rows match ("12 customers"). With none, the table says "No customers match", with a Clear filter button. A new filter goes back to page 1, and only the latest answer counts: number the requests, or abort the previous one. Rows the filter hides stay selected, and the selection toolbar counts them with the rows on other pages. Optional: filters for single columns, such as a status select, in the same bar above the table, each with a visible label, and a Clear all button. The filter's value can also go in the URL, so a link opens the same view.
implementationDetails.pages: Below the table: Previous and Next, page numbers from 768 px, a "Rows per page" select (10, 25, 50, or 100), and a summary ("Showing 11–20 of 245"). Previous on the first page and Next on the last use aria-disabled="true" and ignore presses. The native disabled attribute on a focused Next, as the last page loads, drops focus to the page (checked in Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit). The current page's button has aria-current="page", and page buttons are named with the word ("Page 3"), visible or visually hidden. The status region says the new summary after a page change. If the page scrolls to the table's top, focus moves there too, to the caption or the table's heading (tabindex="-1"); otherwise the scroll position stays. A new page size goes back to page 1. The page and its size can go in the URL. With pages on the server, send the page and the size, and show the total the server returns.
implementationDetails.selection: Each row has a checkbox named after the row ("Select Émile Zola"), and the header has one for the page ("Select all customers on this page"). The checkbox is the one control: rows get neither tabindex nor aria-selected, which belong to the grid pattern. The selection is kept by row id across pages and the filter. The header checkbox shows only this page: checked when every row on it is selected, and partly checked (indeterminate, read as "mixed") when some are. Optional: Shift and a click selects the rows between the last one clicked and this one. Keyboard users check rows one at a time. The selection toolbar's space is reserved above the table, so rows don't move under the pointer when it appears. It says how many rows are selected and how many of them aren't on this page ("5 selected, 2 not on this page"), with Clear selection and the bulk actions, named with the count ("Delete 5 customers"). Delete asks first or offers undo, as the Modal Dialog guide describes. Optional: after the page is selected, the toolbar offers "Select all 245 customers".
implementationDetails.states: While loading, skeleton rows keep the table's shape and are hidden from screen readers (aria-hidden="true"); the status region says "Loading customers…". The header stays. Empty, the table says why, with the next step: "No customers yet" with the action that adds one, or, with a filter, "No customers match" with Clear filter. On an error, the table shows a message and Retry, in text. Server errors and stack traces stay in the logs. Each table keeps its own loading, empty, and error states, so it still works on its own.
implementationDetails.phones: Below 768 px, rows can become cards in a list (<ul>), each card's fields a description list (<dl>), with the row's name as the card's heading. The checkboxes stay, named after their rows; sorting moves to a "Sort by" select, and pagination to Previous and Next. When the columns need to be compared side by side, keep the table, scrolling in its region, instead.
implementationDetails.stickyHeader: Optional: a sticky header row. Inside the horizontal scroll region, it doesn't stick to the page, since the region is its scroll container (checked in Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit). Use one per table: a sticky header without sideways scrolling, with top at the height of any sticky bar above it, or a region with a maximum height that scrolls both ways.
implementationDetails.variations: Row details: a disclosure button in the row ("Show details for Émile Zola") with aria-expanded, and the details in the next row, across all columns. Editing in cells is the grid pattern, beyond this guide; editing in a form or a dialog keeps the table plain. Reordering rows or columns, or resizing columns, by dragging needs a way without dragging (WCAG 2.2 2.5.7), such as Move up and Move down buttons, or a width setting.
implementationDetails.appearance: Suggested defaults; the project's design and tokens win. Rows are 48 to 52 px tall, with 12 to 16 px of padding in each cell. Text meets 4.5:1; sort icons, checkbox edges, and focus indicators 3:1. The current page's button can be #2563eb with white text (5.2:1); #3b82f6 is only 3.7:1. Muted text can be #6b7280 (4.8:1 on white); #9ca3af is 2.5:1. Check the project's own colors. A selected row is marked by its checkbox and a background, not by color alone.

edgeCases.oneRow: With one page, the pagination can go; the summary stays.
edgeCases.manyColumns: The table scrolls in its region, or less important columns hide on smaller screens (hideBelowPx), never the row header.
edgeCases.largePages: For thousands of rows, use pages or render only part of the rows; with partly rendered rows, give the table aria-rowcount and each row aria-rowindex.
edgeCases.selectionAndSorting: Sorting keeps the selection; rows move with their checkboxes.
edgeCases.deletedRows: Rows deleted elsewhere drop out of the selection when the next page arrives.

must: Build on the project's table component or table library when it has a suitable one, and keep its API
Keep it a real table, with a caption, column headers, and row headers
Put a button inside each sortable th, and aria-sort on the sorted column only
Keep the selection by row id, and show only this page in the header checkbox
Use the project's framework version, styling system, and tokens, the way existing components do
mustNot: Add a dependency, such as a table or virtualization library, without asking
Make rows focusable, or put aria-selected on rows of a plain table
Put aria-sort="none" on every unsorted column
Use the disabled attribute on Previous or Next
Show server errors or stack traces in the table
Use inline styles for static values in a plain-CSS project, or hardcode colors the project has tokens for

testingChecklist: It's a table with a caption, column headers with scope="col", and a row header for the cell that names each row
Sortable columns have a button inside the header, and aria-sort is on the sorted column only
Numbers sort as numbers, dates by their value, and text by language with Intl.Collator, and the status region says how the table is sorted
The filter field is labelled; a new filter goes back to page 1, only the latest answer counts, and the number of matches is said once typing pauses
Previous and Next at the ends use aria-disabled, so focus stays on them, and the current page has aria-current="page"
If a page change scrolls to the table, focus moves to the table too
Each row's checkbox is named after its row, and rows aren't focusable themselves
The header checkbox shows only this page: checked when all its rows are selected, mixed when some are
The selection is kept across pages and the filter, and the toolbar says how many selected rows aren't on this page
The toolbar's space is reserved, so rows don't move when it appears, and Delete asks first or offers undo
A wide table scrolls inside a named region with tabindex="0", and the page doesn't scroll sideways
Skeleton rows are hidden from screen readers, and empty and error states say what happened in text, with Clear filter or Retry
On phones, rows are cards in a list with their fields in a description list, or the table scrolls in its region
Styles come from the project's styling system and tokens
